name: The City and its Literatures
description: The course will discuss a range of writings on cities in order to analyze how new urban infrastructures and technologies, newer forms of global capital, majoritarian politics and an increasingly precarious ecological balance have shaped contemporary narratives. In what ways do writings engage the charged times and spaces of the present? In what ways are they different from the 'classic' European city-texts of a century ago, or post- independence literature on the subject from South Asia? How does the tense contestation in our cities over space, place, identity and the past shape and transform what we write and how we read today?
